EigenEngine

Eigen keeps a record of every document a team's AI agents read and every answer they gave, so any answer can be traced back to the documents behind it. The agents reach the documents only through Eigen. EigenEngine Ltd builds it. Pre-release: write to eigen@gmccaul.co.uk to see it.

What it keeps

The record outlasts the conversation

Conversations, drafts and decisions usually disappear when a session with an AI ends. Eigen keeps them as a record in which every claim carries its receipt, and the finished documents are grown from that record.

What that saves

Twelve questions, three ways to start

Twelve questions about one repository, answered three ways. Starting from the record cost 8,408 tokens. Reading the repository's guide files cost eleven times more and answered fewer of the questions. Reading two more files answered them all, at nineteen times the price.

What a question opens

About one document in eighty is opened per question

A question opens 130 to 177 of the 12,335 documents in the repository. The rest are never sent to the model provider, so they are never paid for.

Where it runs

It runs on your machine and calls your own model provider

Eigen runs on a machine inside the customer's environment. The documents, the index built over them and the record stay there. What goes out is the text of each request, to the customer's own model provider, and fewer of them than before.

See it

The index of one paper

The index Eigen built for a paper on a quantum-control algorithm it wrote in July 2026. Each definition, claim, result and limitation in the paper is a node; the lines are the links between them. Hover or tap a node to read it.

91 nodes, 140 links, 6 definitions no claim uses.
Benchmark

SuperARC

A published benchmark asks for the rule behind each of one hundred short binary sequences. Eigen ran a language model with a code sandbox that checked every candidate rule before it could be submitted. 96 of its 100 answers were rules; the published models mostly restated the sequence.

Open the benchmark → Generated paper

Optical twinning trees

In July 2026 a physicist gave Eigen one research question. Over two days Eigen produced a 14-page paper and a 15-slide talk, reviewed its own first draft, and produced a second version. The conversation, including the physicist's corrections, is kept.
